insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: ₹3L to ₹50L (as per grids shown in document; exact SI as per Policy Schedule)

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: “Enhanced Annual Sum insured for Road Traffic Accidents... the Annual Sum Insured shall be doubled... The enhanced (double) Sum Insured shall be available only after exhaustion of the annual sum insured”
great.reference: Base Cover, Clause 16. Enhanced Annual Sum insured for Road Traffic Accidents
great.explanation: For Road Traffic Accidents, the Annual Sum Insured is doubled after the base Annual Sum Insured is fully exhausted. This gives extra insurer-funded cover for large accident claims once your regular limit is used up.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: “In the event of a Claim under the Policy during any subsequent Policy Year, the accrued loyalty bonus shall not be reduced”
great.reference: Base Cover, Clause 13. Loyalty Bonus (point ix)
great.explanation: The accrued loyalty bonus is not reduced even if you make a claim in a later policy year. This helps your increased Sum Insured stay intact instead of dropping after a claim.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED)... shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy”
good.reference: Exclusions, 1. Standard exclusions Code-Excl01: Pre-Existing Diseases
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 24 months of continuous coverage from the first policy inception. This is a standard waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: “specified diseases/treatments... excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with us.”
good.reference: Exclusions, 2. Code-Excl02: Specified disease/procedure waiting period
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are covered only after 24 months of continuous coverage. This is a common market-standard waiting period.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident”
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered for the first 30 days from policy start, except for accidents. This is the usual initial waiting period clause.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “We will cover the Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses... for up to 60days immediately before the Insured Person’s Admission”
good.explanation: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for up to 60 days immediately before admission. This helps pay for tests and consultations leading up to hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “We will cover the Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses... for up to 180 days immediately following the Insured Person’s discharge”
good.explanation: Post-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for up to 180 days after discharge. This supports follow-up treatment and medicines during recovery.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: “We will reset the Annual Sum insured up to 100%... unlimited times, for all future claims within the same policy not related to the illness/disease/injury for which a claim has been paid”
good.explanation: The Annual Sum Insured is reset by up to 100% an unlimited number of times, but only for future claims unrelated to the earlier paid claim. This can increase total coverage in a year, but won’t help if the same illness recurs.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: “We will cover the expenses up to the Annual sum insured incurred on air ambulance services...”
good.explanation: Air ambulance expenses are covered up to the Annual Sum Insured. This can be valuable for emergency transfers when medically required.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: “Room Rent up to Twin sharing room (for Annual Sum Insured below Rs. 10 Lacs and Single private AC room for annual sum insured Rs. 10L and above)”
bad.explanation: Room eligibility is capped to Twin sharing for Sum Insured below ₹10 lakhs and Single private AC room for ₹10 lakhs and above. Taking a higher category room can increase your out-of-pocket costs and may trigger proportional deductions.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: “If the Insured Person is admitted in a room category/limit that is higher... then the Insured Person shall bear a rateable proportion of the total Associated medical expenses...”
bad.explanation: If you choose a room category higher than your eligible limit, you must bear a rateable proportion of associated medical expenses. This can significantly reduce the claim payout beyond just the room rent difference.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “This policy will be subject to 50% base co-payment and He/She shall be liable to pay 50% of admissible claim amount of each and every claim.”
bad.explanation: A 50% co-payment applies, meaning you must pay 50% of the admissible amount for each and every claim. This is a major cost-sharing clause that can halve the effective benefit of the policy.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Below are the non-payable items applicable in the policy... 56 GLOVES... 60 MASK... 57 NEBULISATION KIT...”
bad.reference: General Terms and Clauses, Clause 29. Non Payables (List of Non Payable Items)
bad.explanation: Many consumables and non-payable items (e.g., gloves, masks, nebulisation kit) are excluded from reimbursement. These costs can add up during hospitalization and will typically be paid by you.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: “The expenses payable... for treatment of the following diseases/ conditions... shall be maximum up to the amount mentioned in the table below;”
bad.reference: Base Cover, Clause 15. Sub-limits applicable (A and B tables)
bad.explanation: Certain diseases/conditions have maximum payable limits as per the sub-limit tables, regardless of your overall Sum Insured. This can materially cap payouts for those listed treatments.

bad.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
bad.quote: “We shall not be liable to pay... under this Benefit... Asthma... Arthritis... Diabetes... Hypertension... Pyrexia...”
bad.reference: Base Cover, Clause 7. Domiciliary Hospitalization (exclusions a-k)
bad.explanation: Domiciliary hospitalization has exclusions for several common conditions like asthma, arthritis, diabetes and hypertension. This reduces the usefulness of home-treatment cover for many frequent chronic illnesses.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
